name: Butter Chicken Pasta

ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz dry short pasta (penne, rigatoni or rotini)

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step; no orphans and no invented ingredients. Verified list-vs-steps both directions.

Batch is a clean 3.5x scale of the ~4-serving source (pasta 300g->1050g, chicken 450g->1575g, tomato sauce 2->7 cups, half and half 1->3.5 cups, almond butter 2->7 tbsp, each spice 1tsp->3.5tsp). Internally consistent.
Minor rounding note, not a defect: red pepper flakes at 3.5x of 1/4 tsp would be 0.875 tsp; locked view shows 3/4 tsp. Within normal rounding, flagging for transparency only. Leaving it alone.

No cost_ps was provided in the locked view, so prose uses only the ${{cost_ps}} token and the $1/month membership line. shop_smart makes no per-ounce or lasts-N-batches numeric claim because no cost_lines were supplied to trace one to.
Band check passed on locked figures: 630 cal (in 450-800), 40.2 g protein (>=40), pasta as the real carb source, protein is boneless skinless chicken breast.

Almond butter (a scant 1/2 cup) is the source recipe's stand-in for the cashew/nut base of traditional butter chicken; kept it faithful. Half and half is used, not heavy cream, so prose says half and half.

prose.intro_html:
Butter chicken is one of those restaurant orders that feels like a treat and costs like one too. This is that same warm, spiced, faintly sweet tomato and cream sauce, except it is wrapped around a pot of pasta instead of served over takeout rice, and it feeds fourteen containers out of one pan. The chicken is lean breast, the spice rack does the heavy lifting, and a couple spoonfuls of almond butter give the sauce that nutty, rounded body that makes real butter chicken taste like more than the sum of its parts.

Here is the honest part. This is not a museum-piece butter chicken and it does not pretend to be. It is a weeknight fusion built to hit real numbers: over 40 grams of protein a serving, a genuine carbohydrate on the plate, and a total cook time that fits inside half an hour. You get the flavor you were craving and a fridge full of lunches, and your wallet never feels the difference.
prose.shop_smart:
The spendy line here is the chicken breast, so let that decide your trip. Buy the largest boneless skinless pack you can use, because the big-bag price per pound is almost always kinder than the tidy little tray, and this batch wants three and a half pounds of it. Everything else in the cart is cheap and shelf-stable.

The spice list looks long until you notice it is your standard warm-curry lineup: garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Buy these from the bulk bins if your store has them and scoop only what you need instead of paying for a full jar of something you use by the teaspoon. If you buy jars, you are set for many batches to come, so the cost spreads out fast.

Passata, or plain tomato sauce, is the backbone here and it comes cheap by the jar, so grab a size that covers the full seven cups in one shot rather than opening three little cans. Half and half stands in for the traditional cream and pours a lighter, cheaper pool of dairy while still finishing the sauce silky. The almond butter is the sleeper move: a scant half cup does the job of a lot of pricier ingredients, and the rest of the jar is breakfast tomorrow.
prose.make_it:
Start the pasta first. Boil your short pasta to al dente by the package directions, and before you drain it, dip out a cup or two of that starchy water and set it aside. That water is your sauce insurance, so do not skip it.

While the pasta goes, heat the olive oil and butter together in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chicken pieces and let them cook until they are golden on all sides. Now stir in the diced onion, garlic, and ginger and keep them moving for two to three minutes until softened.

Here is where the kitchen starts to smell like the restaurant. Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, and red pepper flakes, and cook for one minute, stirring constantly so the spices bloom without scorching. Stir in the tomato paste and the tomato sauce and combine. If it looks too thick, loosen it with a splash of that reserved pasta water.

Stir in the almond butter until it melts into the sauce, then pour in the half and half. Bring it up to a boil, drop the heat, and simmer four to five minutes until it thickens. Add the cooked pasta to the pan and toss until every piece is coated. Finish with a good handful of chopped fresh cilantro, season with salt and pepper to taste, and it is done.
prose.portion_html:
This makes fourteen servings, and the way to hit fourteen honestly is to weigh, not eyeball. Once the pasta is tossed and the pan comes off the heat, set your empty container on the scale and zero it out. Weigh the full pan, subtract the pan if you like precise math, then divide the finished weight by fourteen. That number is your target per container.

Scoop to that weight, not to how full the box looks, because the sauce settles and a scoop that looks generous early leaves you short at the end. Level fourteen equal containers and you have fourteen lunches that all carry the same over-40-grams-of-protein hit. A little extra chopped cilantro on top as you portion keeps them looking fresh all week.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Run the register tape and this one lands at ${{cost_ps}} a serving for a full plate: lean chicken, a real carbohydrate, and a spiced cream sauce that tastes like you ordered out. At {{cal}} calories and over 40 grams of protein, you are not choosing between cheap and satisfying, you are getting both in the same box.

That is the whole Thrifty Crew argument in one pan. The takeout version of this dish costs more than the entire fourteen-serving batch, and this one sits in your fridge ready to reheat.

head.description: Butter Chicken Pasta for meal prep: lean chicken breast in a spiced tomato and cream sauce tossed with pasta, 14 servings at over 40 grams of protein each, ready in 30 minutes.

steps: Cook the short pasta to al dente by the package directions. Before draining, reserve a cup or two of the starchy pasta water and set it aside.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add the bite-sized chicken breast pieces and cook until golden on all sides.
Stir in the diced onion, garlic, and ginger. Cook for two to three minutes until softened.
Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, and red pepper flakes. Cook for one minute, stirring constantly so the spices bloom.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomato sauce and combine. Loosen with a splash of reserved pasta water if it looks too thick.
Stir in the almond butter until melted, then add the half and half. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer four to five minutes until thickened.
Add the cooked pasta to the pan and toss until fully coated in the sauce.
Stir in the chopped fresh cilantro, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and serve.
